topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture within the cancer course and sets out its intended learning outcomes.

topics.label: Cancer evolution and the origins of cancer susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations can generate cancerous clones and why their emergence depends on the cells and conditions in which mutations occur.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risks and their interpretation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence that environmental exposures influence cancer risk and how that evidence should be interpreted rather than attributed simply to bad luck.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections contribute to cancer, using Burkitt lymphoma to develop the connection between infection and malignant transformation.

topics.label: Environmental exposures that damage DNA
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how environmental agents produce DNA damage that can become mutations, with their effects depending on biological processing and repair.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish why mutagenic initiation may require a growth-promoting environment before tumours develop.

topics.label: Tissue and developmental susceptibility to carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how carcinogenic effects depend on the biological context of exposure and conclude by recapping the mechanisms underlying that dependence.

topics.label: Methods and limitations of linking exposures to cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how carcinogenic effects can be investigated and what limits the conclusions drawn from the resulting evidence.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarising its conclusions and framing everyday exposure decisions as a balance of risks and benefits.
